$$P(0|x) = \frac{-2x+1}{2}$$

What is the Bayes error of the Bayes classifier relating to this model if $x$ is uniformly distributed on $[-1,1]$?

content:
Consider the Bayes classifier with posterior probabilities:

$$p(1|x) = \begin{cases} 0.5(x+ 1) & x \in [-1,0] \\ 0.5(1-x) & x \in [0,1] \end{cases}$$

$$p(0|x) = 1 - p(1|x)$$

What does it predict for $x$?

answers.content: 1 for all $x \in [-1,1]$
0 for $x > 0$
1 for $x > 0$
0 for all $x \in [-1,1]$

Consider the (unnormalized) Gaussian kernel defined on $R^d$ by $$k(x,z) = \exp\Big(-\frac{||x-z||^2}{2\sigma^2}\Big)$$

Let $\theta$ be a feature mapping and define a modified similarity function:

$$k_{tilde}(x,z) = \exp\Big(-\frac{||\theta(x)-\theta(z)||^2}{2\sigma^2}\Big)$$

Which of the following statements about $k_{tilde}$ is correct?

answers.content: For any choice of mapping $\theta$, $k_{tilde}$ is always a positive semidefinite kernel.
$k_{tilde}$ is a positive semidefinite kernel only when $\theta$ is a polynomial feature mapping.
$k_{tilde}$ defines a positive semidefinite kernel only under additional conditions on $\theta$.

Consider PAC learnability for a hypothesis $h_S \in \mathcal{H}$ trained on a sample $S$, with guarantee:

$$Pr(R(h_S) \le \epsilon) \ge 1 - \delta$$

If this bound holds for $\epsilon=0.1$ and $\delta=0.05$, which of the following claims is true?

answers.content: We are interested in an expected accuracy of 95%.
With probability at least 95%, the generalization error of $h_S$ is at most 10%.
With probability at most 5%, the generalization error of $h_S$ is at most 10%.
For every possible training sample $S$, the generalization error of $h_S$ is at most 10%.
